title: Slow Cooker Chicken, White Bean & Tomato Stew
description: Chicken, white beans, tomatoes, and carrots simmer into a low-effort slow-cooker dinner with ordinary pantry ingredients.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts

substitutions: Use cannellini, great northern, or navy beans.
Use frozen sliced carrots without thawing.
Stir in baby spinach during the final 10 minutes if you have some.

steps.text: Cook until the chicken is tender, then shred and finish.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 pounds chicken, 2 cans drained white beans, 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 cups carrots, 2 cups chicken broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW about 6 hours, until the chicken is fully cooked and tender.
Shred or break up the chicken directly in the cooker, stir well, taste, and season if needed before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Sheet-Pan Cauliflower, Chickpea & Cheddar Bowls
description: Roasted cauliflower and chickpeas get a cheddar finish for an easy meatless sheet-pan meal that works over rice or on its own.
substitutions: Use broccoli florets instead of cauliflower.
Use white beans instead of chickpeas, drying them well before roasting.
Serve with toast instead of rice.

steps.text: Melt cheddar over the top and serve.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 head cauliflower and 1 can chickpeas with 2 tablespoons oil and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder on a large sheet pan.
Roast 20 minutes, stirring once, until the cauliflower is tender and browned at the edges.
Sprinkle 1 cup shredded cheddar over the pan and return to the oven for 3–5 minutes, until melted.
Divide into bowls and serve over up to 2 cups cooked rice if using.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven, air fryer, or microwave until hot.

title: Leftover Spaghetti Pizza Frittata
description: Leftover sauced spaghetti gets folded into eggs, mozzarella, and simple pizza seasoning for a quick skillet rescue meal.

ingredients.item: leftover cooked spaghetti with tomato sauce

substitutions: Use leftover short pasta with tomato sauce instead of spaghetti.
Use cheddar or Monterey Jack instead of mozzarella.
Add a handful of chopped spinach if you want extra vegetables.

steps.text: Mix the leftover pasta with eggs and cheese.
Set the bottom, then finish under the broiler.

cookSteps.text: Turn the broiler on. Beat 5 eggs with 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning, then stir in 2 cups leftover spaghetti and 1/2 cup of the mozzarella.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil or butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the pasta mixture and cook without stirring for 6–8 minutes, until the edges and bottom are set.
Top with the remaining 1/4 cup mozzarella and up to 2 tablespoons Parmesan. Broil 2–4 minutes, watching closely, until the center is set and cheese is bubbly.
Rest 2 minutes, then cut into wedges.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat wedges until hot in a skillet, microwave, or toaster oven.

title: Small-Batch Blueberry Lemon Oat Crumble
description: A little dish of blueberries bakes under a buttery oat topping for a simple fruit dessert sized for a few servings.
substitutions: Use mixed berries instead of blueberries.
Use bottled lemon juice if that is what you have.
Add 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon to the topping if you like.

steps.text: Season the berries and make the oat topping.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put 2 cups blueberries in a small baking dish and toss with 1 tablespoon lemon juice and 2 tablespoons granulated sugar.
Mix 1/2 cup oats, 1/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup brown sugar, and 3 tablespoons butter until crumbly. Scatter evenly over the berries.
Bake 22–25 minutes, until the fruit bubbles around the edges and the topping is lightly browned.

storage: Cover and refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat briefly or eat chilled or at room temperature.
